tips.title: Thinning Vallejo Model Air vs Model Color
tips.text: Thin Vallejo Model Air 2:1 with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for optimal flow. For Model Color, start at a 1:1 ratio, adjust until it flows like syrup. Add 3-5 drops of Vallejo Airbrush Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint. Airbrush at 15-20 psi (1.0-1.5 bar). Test on a paper towel — Model Air should create thin lines, Model Color thicker lines.

tips.title: Base Coat Technique with Tamiya Sprays
tips.text: Shake Tamiya spray cans well before use. Hold 10-12 inches away from the model, spraying side-to-side in even passes. Apply 3-4 light coats, allowing 15-20 minutes drying time between coats. Use 600-800 grit sandpaper to lightly smooth between coats if desired. Finish with a light sanding using 1000-1200 grit wet/dry sandpaper.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Eduard Masks
tips.text: Pre-cut Eduard masking sheets are great for precise camouflage patterns. Apply with soapy water using a soft brush, gently pressing down to remove air bubbles. Allow to dry for 10-15 minutes. Apply paint, using Vallejo Air as preferred. Once dry, carefully peel off masks.

tips.title: Applying Washes — AK Interactive vs AMMO
tips.text: AK Interactive washes are more opaque than AMMO. Use AK Interactive washes neat, applying with a soft brush, allowing to pool in recesses. For AMMO, thin 1:1 with Lemon Spirit or Isopropyl Alcohol for better control. Remove excess with a damp brush or cotton swab after 5-10 minutes. Allow to dry fully before handling.

tips.title: Chipping Technique with Sponge and AK Interactive Chipping Colors
tips.text: Lightly dip a natural sea sponge into AK Interactive Chipping Colors, gently dabbing onto the model. Focus on areas of high wear. Let dry, then lightly sand with 1200 grit wet/dry sandpaper to remove excess pigment. Apply a light touch of Vallejo Airbrush Gloss Varnish to seal before flat coat.
